title: Situational Awareness
subtitle: The Decade Ahead
pitch: A former OpenAI researcher's book length essay series: count the orders of magnitude, expect AGI around 2027, then an intelligence explosion to superintelligence.

chapters.g: You can see the future first in San Francisco: talk of ever bigger compute clusters, and a small group who see what is coming.

chapters.t: I. From GPT-4 to AGI: Counting the OOMs
chapters.g: Compute, algorithmic efficiency and 'unhobbling' each add orders of magnitude. Counting them suggests AGI by about 2027 is strikingly plausible.

chapters.t: II. From AGI to Superintelligence: the Intelligence Explosion
chapters.g: Millions of automated AI researchers could compress a decade of algorithmic progress into a year or less.

chapters.t: IIIa. Racing to the Trillion-Dollar Cluster
chapters.g: The industrial mobilisation: power plants, chips and enormous data centres.

chapters.t: IIIb. Lock Down the Labs: Security for AGI
chapters.g: Labs are not secure against state hackers, and model weights and secrets need far better protection.
Controlling systems much smarter than us is unsolved, and an intelligence explosion makes it harder.

chapters.t: IIId. The Free World Must Prevail
chapters.g: Superintelligence will give a decisive military and economic edge, so democracies must lead.
He predicts a government AGI project, like the Manhattan Project, by around 2027 or 2028.
What if he is right? A call for 'AGI realism'.

ideas: Count the orders of magnitude: compute, algorithms, unhobbling.
AGI around 2027 is plausible on these trends.
Automated AI research could cause an intelligence explosion.
Security and alignment are urgent and underfunded.

args.a: Straight lines on log plots point to AGI by 2027.
args.c: Critics say trends can bend, and that data, power or algorithmic limits may slow things down.

args.a: The free world must win the race.
args.c: Many safety researchers worry race framing makes everyone cut corners and makes coordination, like Pacing the Frontier, harder.

quotes.text: By the end of the decade, they will be smarter than you or I; we will have superintelligence, in the true sense of the word.

questions: Is racing toward superintelligence a safety strategy or a safety risk?
Compare chapter II with the AI 2027 takeoff forecast. Where do they agree?

o: Counting orders of magnitude of effective compute
quiz.w: OOM means order of magnitude, a factor of ten.

o: Removing limits from models, like adding tools and long thinking
quiz.w: Unhobbling unlocks capabilities models already have.
